## Frequently asked questions

**What is orthorexia?**

Orthorexia is an unhealthy obsession with eating only foods perceived as healthy or pure. While it is not yet formally recognized as a diagnosis, it can significantly interfere with daily life and emotional wellbeing. A licensed therapist or psychologist can help you understand whether what you are experiencing fits this pattern and how to address it.

**How do I recover from an eating disorder?**

Recovery typically involves working with behavioral healthcare professionals who understand disordered eating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education to help clients understand and modify their relationship with food. Recovery is a process, and having a compassionate team matters.

**What are the main factors that contribute to eating disorders?**

Eating disorders often develop from a combination of biological, psychological and environmental factors. These can include genetics, trauma, dieting history, cultural pressures around body image, and learned coping patterns. We work with clients to understand their unique contributing factors and build healthier coping skills in a supportive setting.

If you are struggling with disordered eating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

At BCC, we help clients understand these patterns through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education, so they can rebuild a healthier relationship with food.

**How do I stop the urge to overeat?**

Understanding what triggers the urge is the first step. In our program, we work with clients through group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, and mindful eating practices to identify emotional and behavioral patterns. Clients learn practical coping skills and strategies to modify their relationship with food in a compassionate, supportive environment.

**Is binge eating treatment covered by insurance?**

We accept most health insurances, and our claims are processed under mental health benefits. Many clients attend for little to no cost. The Bariatric Counseling Center carries The Joint Commission's Gold Seal of Approval and is in network with most health insurance plans. ## Frequently asked questions

**What is binge eating?**

Binge eating involves consuming large amounts of food in a short period, often feeling out of control during the episode. It may be followed by shame, guilt, or distress. Many people who struggle with binge eating also experience emotional eating or compulsive overeating. A licensed therapist or psychologist can help you understand your relationship with food and develop healthier coping skills.

**How do I stop the urge to overeat?**

Stopping the urge to overeat often requires understanding the emotional, behavioral, and environmental triggers behind it. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful eating education to help clients develop coping skills and modify their relationship with food. Recovery is a process, and our experienced team supports you every step of the way.

**How to psychologically stop overeating?**

Psychological approaches to overeating include identifying emotional triggers, building healthier coping strategies, and practicing mindful eating. We offer behavioral therapy and counseling, dietary guidance, culinary classes, and mindful movement in one comprehensive program. Our team of licensed professional counselors, a clinical psychologist, and registered dietitians works with you to address the root causes of overeating and create sustainable change.

**What to do after eating too much?**

After overeating, focus on self-compassion rather than guilt. Acknowledge what happened without judgment, and consider what triggered the episode. Our program helps clients understand these patterns and build skills to respond differently over time. Behavioral therapy, dietary support, and mindful eating education can help you move forward with greater awareness and control.

If you are ready to get support for compulsive overeating or food addiction, we invite you to reach out to the Bariatric Counseling Center.

We use evidence-based approaches including cognitive behavioral therapy, dialectical behavior therapy, and acceptance and commitment therapy to help clients understand and modify their relationship with food. Our Intensive Outpatient Program combines individual counseling, group therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes, and mindful movement education. **Is medically supervised weight loss covered by insurance?**

Our program is in network with most health insurance plans, and our claims are processed under mental health benefits. Many clients attend for little to no cost. **How does weight loss affect depression?**

We measure changes in anxiety and depression throughout treatment and coordinate care with referring medical providers. Our registered dietitians and licensed counselors work with clients to understand what might be happening and adjust nutrition planning, coping skills, and behavioral strategies. We focus on sustainable changes in your relationship with food rather than short-term results. Your medical provider can also evaluate whether any medical factors are contributing.

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can stem from emotional triggers, stress, boredom, or disordered eating patterns like binge eating disorder. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and group support. A licensed therapist or your medical provider can assess what may be driving your overeating.

**How do I stop the urge to eat all the time?**

We address constant eating urges through our Intensive Outpatient Program, which combines behavioral counseling, recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating work, and mindful eating education. Our registered dietitians and licensed professional counselors work with clients to identify triggers and build sustainable strategies. The work is collaborative, and progress takes time.

**What is an OA meeting?**

Overeaters Anonymous meetings are peer-led support groups based on the 12-step model, where people gather to share their experiences with compulsive overeating and food addiction. Many of our clients attend OA meetings alongside our clinical program. We provide professional behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in a format that complements the peer support OA offers.

**Is Overeaters Anonymous still active?**

Yes, Overeaters Anonymous remains active with meetings worldwide, including in San Antonio. Many people benefit from OA's peer support structure. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we offer clinical treatment for obesity and disordered eating that can work alongside OA participation. Our program includes licensed therapists, registered dietitians, and structured behavioral therapy, serving clients both onsite and virtually throughout Texas.

**What is the premise of Overeaters Anonymous?**

Overeaters Anonymous follows a 12-step model similar to Alcoholics Anonymous, treating compulsive overeating as a condition requiring peer support, spiritual principles, and abstinence from trigger foods. Our approach is clinical and behavioral. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional planning, culinary education, and mindful movement in one program, led by behavioral healthcare professionals. One program, not four.

captions.LI:
You're eating lunch at your desk again.

Not because you planned to. Not because it's the healthier choice. Because that's what the workday asked of you today.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance starts exactly there. Not with a meal plan that pretends your calendar is empty. With the calendar you actually have.

Our registered dietitians work with the rhythm of your real day. The meetings that run long. The commute. The desk lunch. We build nutritional strategies that fit the life you're living, not the one a textbook imagines.

That's part of what makes this program different. Dietary guidance that meets you where you are. Behavioral therapy that helps you understand your relationship with food. Cooking classes that make planning easier. Mindful movement that fits your schedule. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, the Bariatric Counseling Center offers an Intensive Outpatient Program designed for people who struggle with weight loss, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We're in network with most health insurance plans.

Learn more at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/program-schedule.

## Frequently asked questions

**What kind of therapy helps with weight loss?**

Behavioral therapy helps people understand and modify their relationship with food. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy focused on recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating, goal setting, and mindful eating. Our licensed therapists work with clients to address emotional eating, binge eating, and chronic over-eating in a supportive environment.

**What is a weight management doctor for?**

A weight management doctor provides medical treatment for obesity, which may include weight loss medications or bariatric surgery. At BCC, we offer the behavioral healthcare side. Our program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to medical treatment that clients receive from their doctors. We coordinate care with referring medical providers throughout the program.

**What's good for weight management?**

Sustainable weight management requires addressing the behavioral and emotional aspects of eating. We provide behavioral therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. One program, not four. Our Intensive Outpatient Program runs about three months, meeting two to three times per week, and is covered by most health insurance plans.

If you are struggling with weight loss or emotional eating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can mental health providers prescribe GLP-1 medications?**

No. Prescribing weight loss medications is a medical decision made by your physician or nurse practitioner. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and mindful movement to support people taking weight loss medications. We coordinate care with your medical provider but do not prescribe or manage medication.

**Where can I get GLP-1 medication in San Antonio?**

Your primary care physician, endocrinologist or weight management specialist can evaluate whether weight loss medication is right for you. We focus on the behavioral side: helping you build sustainable eating habits, manage emotional eating and understand your relationship with food while you are on medication. We work alongside your medical provider.

**Are there support groups for people on GLP-1 medications?**

Yes. We offer group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education in one Intensive Outpatient Program. Our program serves people struggling with weight loss, binge eating and emotional eating, including those taking weight loss medications. Sessions meet two to three times per week, onsite in San Antonio or virtually across Texas.

**Does insurance cover behavioral support for weight loss medications?**

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a psychological evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

A psychological evaluation assesses whether you are ready for surgery and helps identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect your success. At BCC, our licensed therapist or clinical psychologist conducts a thorough assessment and provides a detailed letter to your surgeon. We also offer ongoing behavioral support through our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**Why do I need a psych eval for bariatric surgery?**

Most surgeons require a psychological evaluation to ensure you are prepared for the lifestyle changes surgery requires. The evaluation looks at your relationship with food, emotional eating patterns, coping skills, and readiness for long-term behavioral change. Your surgeon uses this information to decide if surgery is appropriate and to plan your care.

**What does a psych eval for bariatric surgery look like?**

The evaluation typically includes a clinical interview with a licensed therapist or psychologist, along with written assessments that measure eating behaviors, mood, and quality of life. We review your medical history, weight history, and goals. Afterward, we send a letter to your surgeon with our findings and recommendations for any additional behavioral support you may benefit from.

**Is there an online psychological evaluation available for bariatric surgery?**

Yes. We offer virtual psychological evaluations via telehealth for clients throughout Texas. The evaluation is conducted by video appointment with one of our licensed professionals. Whether you meet with us onsite in San Antonio or virtually, the assessment is the same thorough process, and we provide the documentation your surgeon requires.

**How do I prepare for a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation?**

Be honest and open during the interview. There is no pass or fail. We are looking to understand your relationship with food, your support system, and your readiness for change. Bring a list of any medications you take and be prepared to discuss your weight history, eating patterns, and what you hope surgery will accomplish for you.

If you would like to schedule a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation or learn more about our program, we invite you to reach out.

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I cope with an eating disorder?**

Coping with an eating disorder takes professional support. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education in one comprehensive program. Our licensed therapists and clinical psychologist help clients develop recovery and coping skills, practice intuitive eating, and understand their relationship with food. We work with people struggling with binge eating, compulsive overeating and chronic overeating, both onsite in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

**What eating disorder is most common among men and boys?**

Binge eating disorder is the most common eating disorder among men and boys, though it affects people of all genders. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we treat binge eating disorder and compulsive overeating through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, culinary classes and mindful movement. Our experienced team of licensed professional counselors, a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians provides compassionate, evidence-based care in a supportive environment designed specifically for people who struggle with overeating.

**What are the diagnostic criteria for eating disorders in the DSM-5?**

The DSM-5 lists specific criteria for diagnosing eating disorders, including binge eating disorder, anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to provide a formal diagnosis. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our clinical team includes a licensed psychologist and licensed professional counselors who work with clients struggling with binge eating, emotional eating and chronic overeating. We focus on behavioral treatment and helping clients develop a healthier relationship with food.

If you are struggling with an eating disorder or disordered eating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**How can I train my brain to stop overeating?**

We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, mindful eating education, and dietary guidance from registered dietitians. Our Intensive Outpatient Program teaches recovery and coping skills you can use long after treatment ends. A licensed therapist can work with you on the specific thoughts and behaviors driving overeating.

**How do I stop my cravings and overeating?**

Stopping cravings and overeating takes more than willpower. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful eating education in one program. Our team helps clients build coping skills, set realistic goals, and create a sustainable plan. You work with a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, and registered dietitians who understand the behavioral side of food.

**Why do people binge?**

Binge eating has many causes, including emotional triggers, stress, past dieting, and the way our brains respond to certain foods. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we focus on understanding those patterns and learning new ways to cope. Our behavioral therapy and counseling help clients address the underlying reasons they turn to food, not just the eating itself.

**Where does binge eating start?**

Binge eating often starts with a combination of emotional, environmental, and biological factors. It can develop after years of dieting, during stressful life events, or as a way to manage difficult feelings. We help clients trace those patterns and build healthier responses. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore your individual history and triggers.

If you are struggling with binge eating or chronic overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

captions.FB:
Family engagement in behavioral healthcare for obesity

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, family engagement is part of the work. Not every session, not mandatory, but available when it helps.

A spouse learning how to support without monitoring. A parent understanding the difference between care and control. Adult children finding new ways to talk about food at gatherings.

Family sessions happen when a client asks, or when a counselor suggests it might help move something forward. The people around you don't need to be experts. They just need to understand what you're working on.

We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education in a unique, all-inclusive format. One program, not four. Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

Link in the first comment.
captions.IG:
family support for weight loss and behavioral health

Family engagement is part of the program at the Bariatric Counseling Center. Not every session, not mandatory, but there when it matters.

A spouse learning to support without hovering. A parent shifting from control to care. Adult children finding better ways to navigate holiday meals together.

These sessions happen when a client requests them, or when a counselor sees an opening. The goal is simple. Help the people around you understand the work you're doing, so home becomes easier, not harder.

We offer group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education. One program, not four. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

captions.LI: Many patients receiving medical treatment for obesity benefit from behavioral support alongside their care. The Bariatric Counseling Center is a behavioral health facility focused exclusively on the behavioral treatment of obesity. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. We accept most health insurances. Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. #BehavioralHealth

## What is eating disorder counseling?

Eating disorder counseling is behavioral therapy that helps people understand and modify their relationship with food. It typically involves individual and group sessions with licensed therapists who address disordered eating patterns, including binge eating, emotional eating, and chronic overeating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, we provide eating disorder counseling as part of an Intensive Outpatient Program that combines behavioral therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education. We serve clients onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas. The program is accredited with The Joint Commission Gold Seal and in network with most health insurance plans, with claims processed under mental health benefits.

An eating disorder therapist is a licensed mental health professional who specializes in treating disordered eating patterns, including binge eating, compulsive overeating, and emotional eating. Treatment typically involves individual and group therapy to help clients understand their relationship with food, develop coping skills, and address the psychological factors driving eating behaviors. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, licensed professional counselors and a clinical psychologist provide behavioral therapy as part of an Intensive Outpatient Program that also includes dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes, and mindful movement education. We serve clients onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas, in network with most health insurance plans.

initial.F: Family Engagement: how the program brings the people around a client into the work, gently.
initial.G:
Family engagement in behavioral healthcare for obesity

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, family engagement is part of the work. Not every session, not mandatory, but available when it helps.

A spouse learning how to support without monitoring. A parent understanding the difference between care and control. Adult children finding new ways to talk about food at gatherings.

Family sessions happen when a client asks, or when a counselor suggests it might help move something forward. The people around you don't need to be experts. They just need to understand what you're working on.

We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education in a unique, all-inclusive format. One program, not four. Serving clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

initial.F: Navigating Dining Out from the Dietary Guidance & Support pillar: how the program teaches it, one practical idea, no rules or numbers.
initial.G: Going out to eat doesn't have to feel stressful or lead to a spiral. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, Navigating Dining Out is part of our Dietary Guidance & Support pillar. Our registered dietitians work with clients to build skills that make restaurants feel enjoyable again, not triggering or forbidden. One simple approach: before you go, decide what kind of experience you want. Not what you'll order, but how you want to feel when you leave. Satisfied? Comfortable? Connected to the people you're with? That intention becomes your guide, not a set of food rules. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes and movement education in one program. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. Link in the first comment.

initial.I:
The office candy bowl is not a character test.

Every October it fills up, and for a few weeks a lot of capable people run a private tally at their desks: "Walked past it twice: good. Took three on a deadline: bad". By Friday the tally has turned into a self-shaming verdict: "Guilty".

The candy is not the interesting part. The interesting part is what the afternoon was like when the hand went into the bowl. Tired, behind, under pressure, unfed since 7 a.m. That is information, and it is far more useful than a verdict.

Most of what we teach at the Bariatric Counseling Center starts there: noticing what the urge is responding to, and answering that instead.

GBP.text:
The Bariatric Counseling Center provides intensive outpatient treatment for patients seeking standalone behavioral healthcare for obesity, or as a complement to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications they receive from their medical providers. Our program supports pre-surgical and post-surgical bariatric patients with comprehensive behavioral treatment.

We coordinate care with referring providers throughout treatment. At discharge, we deliver detailed summaries of patient behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression. Treatment updates as requested, typically within two business days.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four. Serving patients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

LI.text:
The Bariatric Counseling Center serves patients seeking standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, as well as those receiving bariatric surgery or weight loss medications from their medical providers.

Our intensive outpatient program supports pre-surgical and post-surgical bariatric patients. We coordinate care with referring providers and deliver detailed discharge summaries of behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

We accept most health insurances. Claims are processed under patients' mental health benefits. Patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Serving patients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

GBP.text:
The Bariatric Counseling Center provides intensive outpatient treatment for patients seeking standalone behavioral healthcare for obesity, or as a complement to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications they receive from their medical providers. Our program supports pre-surgical and post-surgical bariatric patients with comprehensive behavioral treatment.

We coordinate care with referring providers throughout treatment. At discharge, we deliver detailed summaries of patient behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression. Treatment updates as requested, typically within two business days.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four. Serving patients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

Clinical psychologist Dr Sara Hamilton

Dr Sara Hamilton is the Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center. As a clinical psychologist, she leads our behavioral therapy programming for people who struggle with weight-loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic over-eating.

Dr Hamilton works with clients in individual sessions and group therapy, helping them develop recovery and coping skills. Her approach centers on understanding patterns and building sustainable change.

What she wants every new client to know in week one: "You are not alone in your struggles with food! Most clients join our program afraid of group therapy and leave saying that connecting with other people who 'get it' has been an essential part of their healing."

Our team serves clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

LI.text:
When you refer a patient to the Bariatric Counseling Center, you receive consistent coordination throughout their care and a detailed discharge summary at program completion.

Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. We accept most health insurances.

San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

initial.F: Dr Sara Hamilton, Psychologist, Clinical Director. What she wants every new client to know in week one. Needs her one sentence in her own words.
initial.G:
Meet Dr Sara Hamilton, Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center.

Dr Hamilton is a clinical psychologist who leads our behavioral therapy programming. She works with clients one-on-one and in group sessions, helping them understand and modify their relationship with food.

What she wants every new client to know: "You are not alone in your struggles with food!  Most clients join our program afraid of group therapy and leave saying that connecting with other people who 'get it' has been an essential part  of their healing. "

Dr Hamilton leads our experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals serving clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

Link in the first comment.
initial.H:
Clinical psychologist Dr Sara Hamilton

Dr Sara Hamilton is the Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center. As a clinical psychologist, she leads our behavioral therapy programming for people who struggle with weight-loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic over-eating.

Dr Hamilton works with clients in individual sessions and group therapy, helping them develop recovery and coping skills. Her approach centers on understanding patterns and building sustainable change.

What she wants every new client to know in week one:"You are not alone in your struggles with food!  Most clients join our program afraid of group therapy and leave saying that connecting with other people who 'get it' has been an essential part of their healing."

Our team serves clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

#BariatricCounseling #VirtualTherapyTexas #BariatricSupport

Today is Veterans Day. Thank you to every veteran and military family.

Service can leave marks no one else sees, and mental health matters long after the uniform comes off. Asking for support is a sign of strength.

If you need someone to talk to right now, the Veterans Crisis Line is there any time, day or night: dial 988, then press 1, or text 838255.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our licensed mental health professionals and Registered Dietitians work with people whose stress shows up in how they eat, in group and individual therapy. Virtual across Texas.

initial.F: Dr Sara Hamilton, Psychologist, Clinical Director. What she wants every new client to know in week one. Needs her one sentence in her own words.
initial.G:
Meet Dr Sara Hamilton, Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center.

Dr Hamilton is a clinical psychologist who leads our behavioral therapy programming. She works with clients one-on-one and in group sessions, helping them understand and modify their relationship with food.

What she wants every new client to know: "You are not alone in your struggles with food!  Most clients join our program afraid of group therapy and leave saying that connecting with other people who 'get it' has been crucial to healing.

Dr Hamilton leads our experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals serving clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

Link in the first comment.
initial.H:
Clinical psychologist Dr Sara Hamilton

Dr Sara Hamilton is the Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center. As a clinical psychologist, she leads our behavioral therapy programming for people who struggle with weight-loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic over-eating.

Dr Hamilton works with clients in individual sessions and group therapy, helping them develop recovery and coping skills. Her approach centers on understanding patterns and building sustainable change.

What she wants every new client to know in week one: "You're not broken. You're learning a new way to relate to food, and that takes practice."

Our team serves clients on-site in San Antonio and virtually across Texas.

#BariatricCounseling #VirtualTherapyTexas #BariatricSupport

payload.title: Tue 11/24: Referring providers: weight loss medications and the behavioral half
payload.purpose: Patients on weight loss medications (never the drug class abbreviation): the habits that keep the result. Document post.

captions.LI:
Patients on weight loss medications often see dramatic physical results, but lasting change requires the behavioral half: the habits, coping skills, and relationship with food that keep the result after treatment.

The Bariatric Counseling Center provides group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four.

The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medication that patients receive from their medical providers. Our team coordinates care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, we give referring providers a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress during the time in our intensive outpatient program, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. Call it two business days.

We accept most health insurances. Uniquely, the program is in-network with most health insurance plans, and patients typically attend for little to no cost.

Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales: lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200. San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

payload.purpose: The workday eating pattern, without shame, and what dietary guidance in the program does with it.

captions.LI:
You're eating lunch at your desk again.

Not because you planned to. Not because it's the healthier choice. Because that's what the workday asked of you today.

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our dietary guidance starts exactly there. Not with a meal plan that pretends your calendar is empty. With the calendar you actually have.

Our registered dietitians work with the rhythm of your real day. The meetings that run long. The commute. The desk lunch. We build nutritional strategies that fit the life you're living, not the one a textbook imagines.

That's part of what makes this program different. Dietary guidance that meets you where you are. Behavioral therapy that helps you understand your relationship with food. Cooking classes that make planning easier. Mindful movement that fits your schedule. One program, not four.

Serving clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas, the Bariatric Counseling Center offers an Intensive Outpatient Program designed for people who struggle with weight loss, binge eating, and chronic overeating. We're in network with most health insurance plans.

Learn more at bariatriccounselingcenter.com/program-schedule.

captions.FB:
Meet Dr Sara Hamilton, Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center.

Dr Hamilton is a clinical psychologist who leads our behavioral therapy programming. She works with clients one-on-one and in group sessions, helping them understand and modify their relationship with food.

captions.IG:
Clinical psychologist Dr Sara Hamilton

Dr Sara Hamilton is the Clinical Director at the Bariatric Counseling Center. As a clinical psychologist, she leads our behavioral therapy programming for people who struggle with weight-loss, obesity, binge eating, and chronic over-eating.

Dr Hamilton works with clients in individual sessions and group therapy, helping them develop recovery and coping skills. Her approach centers on understanding patterns and building sustainable change.

What she wants every new client to know in week one: "You're not broken. You're learning a new way to relate to food, and that takes practice."

Our team serves clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.
